skill.name: yolo
skill.description: Automates Lovable deployment workflows through MCP or browser automation, including post-push detection, prompt submission, and deployment verification for Supabase backend changes.
skill.summary: Automates Lovable deployment prompts and verification for Supabase backend changes.
skill.author: 10K-Digital

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command and secret-key hits are Markdown examples rather than executable code or embedded credentials. The confirmed risks are the expected external network activity plus semantic risks from auto-deployment, Lovable prompt submission, secret-name inventory, and production endpoint testing. No prompt-injection text was found in the reviewed Markdown files or the visible screenshot content.

remediation.issue: Auto-deploy can run after git push without a fresh per-run approval.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit confirmation before deployment or migration unless a project has a documented approval policy.

remediation.issue: Secret names can be extracted and shown in debug output.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for consent before collecting secret inventory and redact secret names in logs unless the user requests details.

remediation.issue: Deployment prompts and project identifiers are sent to Lovable.
remediation.suggestion: Document external destinations and show what will be submitted before using MCP or browser automation.

remediation.issue: Functional verification can call live Supabase endpoints.
remediation.suggestion: Use safe test payloads, skip side-effecting actions by default, and ask before testing email, payment, or mutation endpoints.

remediation.issue: Browser automation depends on Lovable UI selectors and an unscanned screenshot asset.
remediation.suggestion: Keep selector documentation current and replace screenshots when UI changes are reviewed.

content.value_statement: Manual Lovable deployment steps slow backend releases and create repeat work. This skill submits deployment prompts, monitors results, and runs verification checks.
actual_capabilities: Detects Supabase edge function and migration changes after a successful git push.
Submits Lovable deployment prompts through MCP or browser automation.
Waits for Lovable to sync GitHub changes before deployment prompts.
Runs deployment verification through logs, console checks, and endpoint tests.
Falls back to manual Lovable prompts when automation is unavailable.
Reads Yolo mode settings and Lovable project URLs from CLAUDE.md.
limitations: Requires a configured Lovable project URL and access to the target project.
Browser mode requires the Claude Chrome extension and an active Lovable login.
Automation can break if Lovable changes its UI or MCP behavior.
Production deployments still need human review in controlled environments.

use_cases.title: Ship Supabase Edge Functions
use_cases.description: Deploy changed edge functions through Lovable after code reaches main.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Backend Migrations
use_cases.description: Apply pending migrations before dependent functions are deployed.

use_cases.title: Verify Lovable Releases
use_cases.description: Run post-deployment checks against logs, browser console output, and endpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Enable Yolo Mode
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Lovable project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Enable yolo mode for this Lovable project, use MCP when available, and keep browser automation as fallback.

prompt_templates.title: Deploy One Function
prompt_templates.scenario: Manual deployment of a specific backend change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use yolo mode to deploy the updated send-email edge function, then run the standard verification checks.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Post-Push Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Automated workflow after pushing backend files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the last push for Supabase functions or migrations, then deploy the required Lovable changes if auto-deploy is enabled.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Deployment Readiness
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced preflight before a sensitive release.
prompt_templates.prompt: Before deployment, check required secrets, migration safety, GitHub sync status, and available verification levels. Ask before risky actions.

output_examples.input: Deploy the updated email function with yolo mode.
output_examples.output: The skill reports that it opened the Lovable project, submitted the deployment prompt, confirmed success, and completed verification checks.

output_examples.input: Auto-deploy after a push that changed a migration.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies the migration, waits for Lovable sync, asks for confirmation if the migration may be destructive, and summarizes the result.
The skill explains the failure and provides the exact Lovable prompt for manual submission.

best_practices: Keep auto-deploy disabled for production branches unless your team has approved the workflow.
Use MCP when available because it avoids fragile browser UI selectors.
Review secret requirements and migration safety before enabling unattended deployment.
anti_patterns: Do not use auto-deploy for regulated production changes without a human approval step.
Do not rely on browser mode when Lovable UI changes are likely or untested.
Do not print full secret values in debug logs or deployment summaries.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It automates Lovable deployment prompts, post-push detection, and verification for Supabase backend changes.

faq.question: Does it require Lovable MCP?
faq.answer: No. It prefers Lovable MCP when connected and falls back to browser automation or manual prompts.

faq.question: Can it deploy automatically after git push?
faq.answer: Yes. Auto-deploy runs only when yolo mode and auto-deploy are enabled in the project configuration.

faq.question: Does it read secret values?
faq.answer: The documented workflow extracts secret names and status, not secret values. Debug output should still be reviewed.

faq.question: What can break this skill?
faq.answer: Browser mode can break when Lovable changes page structure, selectors, or login behavior.

faq.question: Is this suitable for production?
faq.answer: It can support production workflows, but teams should add explicit approvals for deployments and migrations.
